title: Rationalize accent system and proportional elevation for scrollable tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our color accent system, radius ramp, and elevation tokens diverge across component families (buttons, cards, scrollable tables). This causes inconsistent visual weight and accessibility regressions in dense surfaces: row separators and hover states rely on different accent variants, shadows for pill buttons look stronger than card shadows at the same elevation step, and press depth is inconsistent across touch and desktop.

Goal: Introduce a small set of surface-aware tokens and a proportional elevation multiplier so that accents, shadows, and press-depth values scale predictably across compact and regular density components. The scope focuses on scrollable data tables and related controls (row actions, sticky headers, inline buttons) but must be compatible with other surface types (cards, modals, tooltips).

Outcomes: a) A stable palette subset for interactive accents usable in light/dark; b) a proportional elevation ramp (multipliers + surface anchors) that preserves contrast and motion when density changes; c) a migration plan and codemod to update components with minimal visual regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Define a set of 6 accent anchors (accent-anchor-1..6) with accessible contrast on both light and dark tokens
Document a proportional elevation system (elev-surface-1..4 + multipliers for compact/dense modes) with examples for table rows, sticky headers, and inline buttons
Provide Figma tokens and a migration spec; components in the token sandbox match approved visuals within +/-1px and color delta < 2.5 ΔE
Deliver codemod(s) and a staged rollout plan: canary -> internal beta -> GA with rollback plan
Confirm no high-severity accessibility regressions in selected pages (tables, forms, action bars) via axe and manual review
design_notes: Use neutral-tinted accents (warm/cool anchors) rather than saturated swatches for emphasis in dense rows
Separate press-depth from elevation: press-depth is a transient motion/offset token, elevation is a long-lived shadow geometry token
Introduce radius-compact and radius-default tokens; radius-compact should be 60% of radius-default to preserve hit targets while saving space
Shadows use layered blur + offset with a multiplicative intensity factor for compact mode rather than discrete shadow stacks
Preserve developer ergonomics by naming tokens as surface-aware (e.g., accent-anchor--table-hover, elev-surface--sticky-header) but expose canonical base tokens to the theming layer
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Token spec authored in Figma and tokens JSON exported (Design authoring) - due 2026-02-20
Phase 2: Prototype small set of tables in token-sandbox with ember/React components updated to new tokens - collaborate with ENG-19821 - due 2026-03-05
Phase 3: Create codemod to rename/localize old token names to new (run on all repositories) - ENG implements in ENG-19821 branch
Phase 4: Canary rollout behind feature flag to internal apps and telemetry collection for visual diffs and accessibility checks - monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 5: GA and document migration guidelines in the Design System handbook

decisions_made: Adopt accent-anchor tokens instead of individual component-specific accents to reduce token sprawl
Implement proportional elevation via multipliers (1.0 default, 0.7 compact) rather than creating separate discrete elevation stacks for every surface
Introduce radius-compact token and keep radius-default; do not compress hit targets below WCAG guidance
Shadow geometry will be represented as (offset, blur, opacity) triple exposed to theming layer, with a compact multiplier applied at render time
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Visual regressions on legacy pages. Mitigation: Codemod + canary behind feature flag + visual diff tooling (chromatic) before GA
Risk: Performance impact from shadow changes on large scrollable tables. Mitigation: Use GPU-friendly single-pass shadow and limit shadow layers on high-row-count containers
Risk: Confusion from token rename. Mitigation: Provide mapping table and codemod; communicate changes in weekly design sync
qa_checks: Run automated visual diffs for top-15 customer-facing pages (chromatic) and compare delta metrics
Accessibility sweep (contrast, focus order, hit target sizes) for affected components
Manual regression pass on Chrome, Safari, and Firefox at 100% and 150% zoom for density edge cases
Performance smoke test: render large table (5k rows) and measure frame drops before/after shadow change
